topSignals.title: Oracle's largest AI data center just hit a fuel-cell-critical gas pipeline delay — Bloom Energy stock fell ~6-8% and is now a live risk case.
topSignals.text: Oracle sent a force majeure notice on the 2.45 GW, $165B "Project Jupiter" Stargate campus in New Mexico (developed by Blue Owl Capital's Stack Infrastructure) after Energy Transfer's feeder pipeline slipped from an August 2026 target to February 1, 2027 due to New Mexico permitting hurdles; a separate air-quality permit for the Bloom fuel cell system itself is still pending state approval, due by November 23. Oracle and Blue Owl both say the project timeline and financial commitments are unchanged, but the gas-supply gap directly delays when Bloom's fuel cells can actually run, and BE shares dropped roughly 6-10% intraday on Sept 24 on the news. TechCrunch | 24/7 Wall St. | TradingKey

topSignals.title: Germany's EEG-Novelle 2027 and Netzpaket cleared their first Bundestag reading on Sept 24; the Bundesrat reviews the package today, Sept 25.
topSignals.text: The debate centered on eliminating fixed feed-in tariffs for small rooftop PV (≤25 kW) and new curtailment/penalty rules for solar in congested grid zones — reporting reviewed today still gives no explicit detail on how the reform treats larger self-generation/behind-the-meter installations, the category relevant to a German SOFC data-center case. The whole package must clear the full legislative process in October to meet an EU-approval deadline. pv magazine | Bundestag

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new SOFC/data-center news beyond Top Signal #2. Standing status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform, ELCO I Tallinn factory ramping toward 360 MW/yr, Sept 21 Metrosert testing cooperation, Sept 15 Shanghai HyEnergy collaboration.

Topsoe (priority): No new news — ninth consecutive quiet day (Top Signal #2). SOEC-only Herning factory (500 MW/yr) remains the flagship asset; SOFC/data-center pathway still deferred under the May 2026 roadmap review.

Ceres Power: No new developments since the Sept 23/24 H1 2026 results (Doosan's ~£60M Reverion export order, Weichai 200 MW licensee target, data centers ~50% of Ceres's 22 GW TAM — all already logged).
No new stack/cell announcements found from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin in the last 24-48h.

Top story — see Top Signal #1:* Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (New Mexico) is the first concrete sign of schedule risk in Bloom's largest single deployment, driven by a natural-gas feeder-pipeline delay to Feb 2027 and a pending fuel-cell air-quality permit due Nov 23. No other new orders, PPAs or pilots found in the last 24-48h from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle/OpenAI, xAI, or colocation players (Equinix, Digital Realty). Standing pipeline otherwise unchanged: Bloom-AEP, Bloom-Brookfield ($25B), Bloom-Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Bloom-Nebius, Bloom-Aligned "Project Phoenix" (Shippingport, PA), Hitachi-Bloom Japan, FCEL-Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), FCEL-Inuverse Korea, FCEL Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, FCEL-SDCL, Ceres-Centrica, Ceres-Weichai, EU EcoEdge PrimePower (Equinix Milan pilot), Doosan Fuel Cell-HyAxiom KRW 501.4B contract.

Top story — see Top Signal #3:* Germany's EEG-Novelle 2027/Netzpaket passed first reading Sept 24; Bundesrat review today, Sept 25; full passage needed in October for the EU deadline. Separately, the Project Jupiter dispute (Top Signal #1) surfaces a concrete New Mexico regulatory data point: the fuel cell system's own air-quality permit is not yet approved and is due by Nov 23 — a real-world illustration of permitting timelines that matters for SOFC's "fast-to-permit" pitch versus gas turbines. Standing US background unchanged: both federal large-load cost-shift bills (Ratepayer Protection Act, GRID Savings Act) remain dead; PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window opens Sept 30 (through Oct 21); FERC RM26-4 show-cause responses due Nov 16; Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; US ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell credit; New York permit moratorium; Texas development pause; EPA turbine NSPS "temporary" classification (in force since Jan 15, 2026, under legal challenge).

Bloom Energy (BE): Fell roughly 6-10% intraday on Sept 24 (sources range from -6.17% to -10% depending on measurement window) on the Project Jupiter force majeure news — see Top Signal #1. This is a genuine negative catalyst, distinct from the routine scandium-lawsuit and index-rebalancing coverage carried in recent days; Q3 earnings still due Oct 27, and the scandium securities-suit lead-plaintiff deadline is Sept 28.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): No new operational disclosures in the last 24-48h; continued plaintiff-firm reminder press releases for the Nov 10, 2026 lead-plaintiff deadline (Fit Energy cost-overrun disclosure). Backlog remains $3.6B per the Q3 transcript.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new market-moving news since the Sept 23/24 H1 results already logged.

lcoe.text: No new capex/opex/efficiency figures today. Henry Hub carry-forward unchanged: EIA's August 2026 STEO full-year 2026 average estimate remains ~$3.43-3.44/MMBtu; a July 2026 STEO figure of $3.67/MMBtu for 2026 also circulated in search results but is superseded by the more recent August print — no September STEO update was found today, so the $3.43-3.44 figure stands, still below the model's carried $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption and worth reconciling.

Permitting-timeline datapoint (qualitative, not a cost figure): the Bloom/Oracle Project Jupiter fuel-cell air-quality permit is still pending New Mexico state approval with a Nov 23 deadline, and the site's gas feeder pipeline slipped roughly six months (Aug 2026 → Feb 2027) — a concrete, dated illustration of permitting/infrastructure lead-time risk to weigh against SOFC's usual "~90-day build" framing when modeling deployment schedules.

Pending calendar: Bundesrat EEG-Novelle/Netzpaket review (today, Sept 25), Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), New Mexico air-quality permit deadline for Project Jupiter fuel cells (Nov 23), FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 10), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27).
